relevance_reason: The paper describes vitelliform macular dystrophy caused by IMPG1 and IMPG2 mutations. This is an allelic disorder of IMPG2, not retinitis pigmentosa, so it gives context only for the RP56 entry.

findings.statement: Meunier et al. (2014) screened IMPG1 and IMPG2 in 49 families with vitelliform macular dystrophy who had no identified BEST1 or PRPH2 mutation. In 1 family (2 patients) with autosomal dominant vitelliform macular dystrophy, they identified a c.3230G-T mutation in IMPG2, resulting in a cys1077-to-phe (C1077F) substitution. IMPG1 was the causal gene in 3 other families. Overall, the authors estimated that IMPG1 and IMPG2 account for 8% of families negative for BEST1 and PRPH2 mutations.
quotes: IMPG1 was the causal gene in 3 families (IMPG1 1-3, 11 patients) and IMPG2 in a fourth family (2 patients).
family 4 had the c.3230G→T (p.Cys1077Phe) mutation in IMPG2
IMPG1 and IMPG2 are new causal genes in 8% of families negative for BEST1 and PRPH2 mutations.

findings.statement: Meunier et al. (2014) reported that the 13 patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 mutations had late-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy with moderate visual impairment (mean age of onset, 42 years; mean visual acuity, 20/40). Drusen-like lesions next to the vitelliform deposits were seen in 9 of the 13 patients. On spectral-domain OCT, the vitelliform material lay above the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and the RPE was well preserved with normal reflectivity. Electro-oculogram results were normal or borderline in 9 cases.
quotes: Patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 mutations had a late onset and moderate visual impairment (mean visual acuity, 20/40; mean age of onset, 42 years)
Drusen-like lesions adjacent to the vitelliform deposits were observed in 9 of 13 patients.
Electro-oculogram results were normal or borderline in 9 cases.

relevance_reason: The paper identifies IMPG2 mutations as the cause of autosomal recessive RP, which is the defining finding for RP56.

findings.statement: Using autozygosity mapping, Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) identified 2 families, each with 3 affected sibs with retinitis pigmentosa. The affected sibs shared large overlapping homozygous regions on chromosome 3 that contained the IMPG2 gene.
quotes: Using autozygosity mapping, we identified two families, each with three affected siblings sharing large overlapping homozygous regions that harbored the IMPG2 gene on chromosome 3.

findings.statement: In 3 affected sibs of Iraqi Jewish ancestry with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa, Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) found a homozygous nonsense mutation in the IMPG2 gene. The mutation cosegregated with the disease in the family.
quotes: Sequence analysis of IMPG2 in the two index cases revealed homozygous mutations cosegregating with the disease in the respective families: three affected siblings of Iraqi Jewish ancestry displayed a nonsense mutation

findings.statement: In a Dutch family with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa, Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) found a homozygous 1.8-kb genomic deletion in the IMPG2 gene that removes exon 9. The deletion leads to the loss of 7 amino acids in a conserved SEA domain and cosegregated with the disease. In transfected COS-1 cells, the wildtype SEA domain was targeted to the plasma membrane, but the mutant lacking the 7 amino acids appeared to be retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.
quotes: a Dutch family displayed a 1.8 kb genomic deletion that removes exon 9 and results in the absence of seven amino acids in a conserved SEA domain of the IMPG2 protein
a construct expressing the wild-type SEA domain is properly targeted to the plasma membrane, whereas the mutant lacking the seven amino acids appears to be retained in the endoplasmic reticulum

variants.as_reported: 1.8 kb genomic deletion that removes exon 9

findings.statement: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) analyzed IMPG2 in 10 additional index cases of Dutch, Israeli, Italian, and Pakistani origin whose homozygous regions included IMPG2. They found 5 additional mutations: 4 nonsense mutations and 1 missense mutation that affects a highly conserved phenylalanine residue.
quotes: Mutation analysis in ten additional index cases that were of Dutch, Israeli, Italian, and Pakistani origin and had homozygous regions encompassing IMPG2 revealed five additional mutations; four nonsense mutations and one missense mutation affecting a highly conserved phenylalanine residue.

variants.as_reported: missense mutation affecting a highly conserved phenylalanine residue

findings.statement: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) reported that most patients with IMPG2 mutations had early-onset retinitis pigmentosa, with visual-field loss and declining visual acuity that both progressed over time.
quotes: Most patients with IMPG2 mutations showed an early-onset form of RP with progressive visual-field loss and deterioration of visual acuity.

findings.statement: Bandah-Rozenfeld et al. (2010) reported that the patient with the IMPG2 missense mutation was diagnosed with maculopathy, not retinitis pigmentosa.
quotes: The patient with the missense mutation, however, was diagnosed with maculopathy.
